hypothesis: H9: making one whole motif fit one lattice cell - by fixing how beadDist samples, rather than by choosing a different motif - makes the bead nameable on the wall.
why: The sampling defect is REAL, was measured exactly, and is now FIXED - and fixing it does not make the bead nameable. GPU-readback probe (scripts/lab-probe.mjs), controller OFF, seeds pinned, full res, coarsest drawn level i=4: current sampling spans texcoord 0.494..1.976 = 1.482 texture periods with 85.1% of pixels wrapping (1.671 periods / 88.98% with lattice-nav ON, matching the reported 1.678). min==0.494 is the damning half: because fractal() passes abs(p), the coordinate never drops below the texture centre, so only the motif's upper-right QUADRANT is ever fetched. After L1+L2 the span is 0.000..0.988 = 0.988 periods with 0% wrap at EVERY drawn level - exactly one whole, unmirrored texture period per cell. LEVER DECOMPOSITION: L1 (unmirror, sample signed p instead of abs(p)) changes 0.36% of pixels - a NO-OP. L2 (in-shader CLAMP_TO_EDGE on the fetch plus an analytic monotone exterior extension) changes 49.3% and does all the work; L2 alone vs L1+L2 differ by 0.09%. L1 being a no-op is not a null result, it is the PROOF of the real blocker: the 4-fold mirror is intrinsic to the fold, not to abs(p). fractal() folds the plane onto [0,1]^2 and draws the cell around p=0, which is a CORNER of the fold domain, so the four screen quadrants around any cell centre map to the SAME fold quadrant. Every function of p is therefore automatically 4-fold mirror-symmetric about a cell centre, which is also why hexDist (which takes abs() internally) was never affected by abs(p) either. Consequence: the lattice can only ever display the FOLD's symmetry, never the motif's, so a 12-lobe kiku, a 5-lobe ume and a 3-comma tomoe are all reduced to the same 4-fold wedge. Measured on the isolated coarsest level (LEVELS=5, ld pinned, sampling fixed, the level the coordinator measured as carrying 92-94% of the bead effect): ume vs tomoe differ by 3.15% of pixels - a five-petal plum blossom and a three-comma swirl render essentially identically. Across the full stack, fixing the sampling did NOT raise between-motif discriminability (32.1% -> 31.5% mean pairwise, ume-vs-tomoe actually fell 29.95% -> 19.82%) and moved the picture CLOSER to the plain hexagon (departure vs hex 52.9% -> 38.4%), because most of the ink the wrap was adding was spurious wrapped-tile lines. BONUS: that also disposes of the brightening counter-ratchet question - the +25% meanLum the bead arms show over hex (13.23 vs 10.69) is the WRAP ARTIFACT; with the sampling fixed meanLum returns to 10.52, essentially the hex baseline (10.69), so no counter-ratchet is needed. VERDICT ON THE GOAL AS STATED: unreachable without rewriting fractal(), which the brief forbids. The fix is still worth keeping - it is correct, it costs nothing, cells now carry closed single contours instead of wrapped scribble, and it removes the spurious brightening - but it is necessary, not sufficient.
cost_to_lattice: None observed. No seams, no broken symmetry, no loss of the kaleidoscopic quality - the fold is untouched and hexDist(abs(p)) is identically hexDist(p), so the hex baseline provably cannot move. The picture is CLEANER (fewer spurious lines) but also less busy, which reads as closer to plain hex: departure from the hex baseline falls 52.9% -> 38.4%. Whether that is a gain or a loss is an aesthetic call for the user, not a measurement.
conditions: Headed Chromium, real GPU, 900x900 fixed viewport, deviceScaleFactor 1, full resolution readPixels off the WebGL2 canvas (never canvas2D). ALL NUMBERS controller OFF (no lattice-nav) with paperCranes.seeds pinned to [0.618,0.755,0.892,0.029] in localStorage AND seed..seed4 in the URL. n=3 over time=4,8,16 with spread stated. Lit-coverage cutoff luma>40 (stated because the magnitude is not threshold-robust). Port asserted per capture by number AND by content: 6987 serves whole.frag containing WHOLE_ONETILE, 6984 (lab/fill) does not, and every arm responded to knob_164, a uniform that exists only in this worktree.
spawned: The lattice can only ever show a symmetry order compatible with the fold's 4-fold mirror. If mon are to stay, the motif library should be filtered to 4-fold/8-fold crests (kikko, hakkaku, matsukawa) rather than the 12/5/3-fold ones currently favoured - or the goal restated as 'the lattice is textured by the bead' rather than 'name the bead'.

The one legitimate route to a nameable motif is to draw ONE cell centred, outside fractal() - e.g. a single un-folded bead layer composited over the lattice. That is an addition, not a rewrite of fractal(), so it does not violate the brief. Untested.

beadDist's exterior is now a proper monotone SDF (clamp + length(tc-tcc)*2 extension). That makes solid-fill mode (d alone, no abs(d-gRingGap)) well-defined for the first time; lab/fill's occlusion finding was measured against the wrapped field and may not hold against the fixed one.
delt2 (the cross term) still uses abs(p) and is drawn on every level; it is the only skeleton element untouched by the bead swap, and at one-level isolation it is most of what remains visible.
onelevel.frag (LEVELS=5, ld pinned to 0) is a cheap and reusable isolation rig for attributing an effect to a single recursion level.
